graves.title: Predictability gap: an in-sample mirage
graves.claim: my deliberate plays are less predictable to the algorithm (d ≈ 0.5–0.6).
graves.killed_by: a chronological holdout: train on the past, test on the future.
graves.result: in-sample d=0.62 → full-vocab held-out d=−0.02 (CI brackets 0); top-600 d=+0.11 = frequent-artist memorization
graves.verdict: it was overfitting. across the full catalog the gap is noise; the sliver that survives on my most-played artists is memorization, not intent.

graves.title: Body drives music: a clock, not a cause
graves.claim: my physiology steers what i play (ρ ≈ 0.36).
graves.killed_by: partialling out the 24-hour sinusoid, plus phase-randomized surrogates.
graves.result: ρ 0.36 → 0.07 · 9 of 11 Granger arrows die under the surrogate
graves.verdict: a shared daily clock generated it. not preference.

graves.title: World→jazz priming: the recommender’s sequencing
graves.claim: world/desi listening primes jazz three weeks later (F=9.09, survives FDR).
graves.killed_by: intent stratification: splitting the series by how each play started.
graves.result: the whole F-stat lives in autoplay auto-advance · null under shuffle
graves.verdict: spotify’s sequencer primes jazz, not my cognition.

graves.title: “i’m choosing more over time”: a logging artifact
graves.claim: deliberate taps rose 13.5% → 22.8% across the whole log.
graves.killed_by: instrumentation forensics: a new back-button code first logged 2023-08, plus a device flip.
graves.verdict: the instrument changed, not me. the cross-sectional results still stand.

graves.title: PELT event attribution, it fires at everything
graves.claim: changepoint detection nailed 5 of 5 known dates.
graves.killed_by: a shuffled-event null, score the hits against permuted dates.
graves.verdict: it catches everything, including events that never happened.

graves.title: A known date, the data didn’t move
graves.claim: a known date should shift listening across 11 behavioral metrics.
graves.killed_by: a pre/post window across all eleven.
graves.verdict: kept anyway, hiding the nulls is how honest analysis turns into selection bias.

graves.title: Run-down days→narrower listening: a season
graves.claim: physiology narrows my listening; it even survives an activity control.
graves.result: ρ +0.42 → +0.34 n.s. · skin-temp −0.55 → −0.15 · 3rd time this pattern showed
graves.verdict: a shared season, not a cause.

graves.title: Music → heart rate: null
graves.claim: genre drives my heart rate (+12.9 bpm, chillstep vs EDM).
graves.killed_by: shuffle-as-instrument: isolate the effect of choice i didn’t make.
graves.verdict: it’s the activity, not the music. gone once the choice is exogenous.

graves.title: Genre trends over time: mostly what was served
graves.claim: my genre mix drifted on its own across the whole log.
graves.killed_by: a moving-block bootstrap plus intent stratification.
graves.result: 0 of 7 families show a real sign-flip
graves.verdict: the platform’s surfacing, not my drift, with one real exception: electronic climbing is genuinely mine.

graves.title: Next-press predictor: the song-features coin flip
graves.claim: i can predict my own next presses from audio + history.
graves.verdict: narrowed 2026-07-19: whatever drives a next press isn’t in the audio; session-sequence features reach 0.815 held-out, and two features (my last press + the session’s next-press rate so far) give 0.80. the spiral predicts; the song doesn’t.

graves.title: Cross-modal prediction: small but real, then zero
graves.claim: a joint model that sees both physiology and listening out-predicts either alone (ΔR² ≈ +0.01).
graves.killed_by: a block bootstrap on the held-out gain, plus a re-fit.
graves.result: ΔR² = −0.002 · 95% CI [−0.011, +0.008] · 60% of resamples favor music-only · sign flips on re-fit
graves.verdict: it survived the circadian partial-out but not the bootstrap. no reliable transfer either way.

graves.title: Taste-shape forecasts churn: the map peeked
graves.claim: an artist’s bridge role in my taste graph predicts whether i drop it next year, beyond how much i played it.
graves.killed_by: a leak-free retrain: rebuild the map from only the past, never the future.
graves.result: forward-test AUC 0.71 → 0.58 leak-free · lift over play-count −0.004
graves.verdict: the embedding was trained on the whole timeline, so it already knew who i’d abandon. blind it to the future and the edge is gone.

graves.title: The portability demo: confidently wrong about 696 strangers
graves.claim: my timing-only intent proxy, frozen, ports to a public 992-user Last.fm log: the recovered “deliberate” plays should look more artist-diverse, like mine do.
graves.killed_by: its own pre-declared directional gate, plus a control that ran the same readout back on my own log.
graves.result: median gap −0.34 · 99% of per-user CIs exclude zero (on the wrong side) · the sign inverts on my log too (−0.22 inferred vs +0.02 true labels)
graves.verdict: the intervals were statistically valid; the construct wasn’t. the proxy keys on session position, and early-session plays stay artist-coherent no matter who chose them. tight confidence intervals around a wrong-signed conclusion, for 696 people at once: exactly the failure class this page exists to catch.

graves.title: The depth story of passivity decay: composition wearing a curve
graves.claim: the deeper autoplay wanders into never-tapped territory, the closer its plays get to preference-free, and over familiar ground, deep streaks are graduated delegation.
graves.killed_by: holding the track fixed: track fixed-effects plus a track-matched conditional logit.
graves.result: familiar “rise”: FE slope −0.00008, CI straddles zero · never-tapped “collapse”: ~8% survives within-track · ~92% = which tracks fill deep streaks
graves.verdict: the curves were real; depth wasn’t the cause. deep streaks reach different tracks; they don’t change a given track’s odds. the levels survive untouched: never-tapped autoplay earns a later tap 7.2% of the time vs 28.7% for music i found myself.

graves.title: The flat 19%: one number over a changing ruler
graves.claim: 19% of my plays were a deliberate tap: one stable number for the whole log.
graves.killed_by: a pre-declared era-stability audit against the logger’s own changepoints.
graves.result: bundled tap-rate: 11.8% → 22.7% across the 2023-10 era boundary · 10.9pp swing vs a <3pp bar
graves.verdict: the instrument moved, not (only) me; the backbtn code entered the vocabulary in 2023, and the device mix flipped. the strict definition (11.5%), the one the Bridge Index actually leans on, swings 1.87pp and survives. pooled scalars over a non-stationary logger need era labels.

graves.title: The 4-year reign “p = 0.0000”: a straw-man null
graves.claim: Phaeleh topping the chart 4 straight years is wildly improbable (p = 0.0000, 10,000 sims).
graves.killed_by: a persistence-preserving null, the same fix the era count already got.
graves.result: identity-rerandomizing null: p = 0.0000 · circular block bootstrap on real monthly hours: p = 0.58 (3-month blocks), 0.49 (12-month), 0.40 (year-permute)
graves.verdict: the original null re-rolled my taste every January. keep persistence (the thing listening actually has) and a 4-year reign is just what a plateau anchor does. the reign is real; the improbability was manufactured.
